page: Microsoft Azure D32as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv5 series. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz, offering 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system is configured with 128.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, though AVX-512 capabilities are not supported on this platform. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring external network block storage for persistent filesystem access.

Benchmark testing reflects balanced performance across compute and memory operations. Single-core throughput places in the top quartile with a stress-ng score of 2702.76, complemented by a strong PassMark memory benchmark score of 2902.55. Multi-core performance is aligned with the middle distribution tier, producing a stress-ng multi-core score of 43243.6 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 14253. Memory bandwidth measures 74.32 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 44.85 GB/sec for uncached writes. In specialized tests, the instance records strong results in image processing tasks and small-model language generation at 319.14 tokens per second, though large-model inference drops significantly due to CPU-only execution.

The absence of local ephemeral NVMe storage necessitates external volume management for workloads with intensive disk I/O demands. However, the combination of dedicated CPU allocation and substantial memory capacity yields solid service performance, reaching 31.78 million Redis SET operations per second and 24.94 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. These characteristics position the D32as_v5 well for enterprise web tiers, intermediate relational databases, continuous integration build agents, and container worker nodes.

The instance includes no local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-core CPU throughput and top-quartile PassMark memory performance, accompanied by consistent middle-tier multi-core execution. The configuration fits enterprise application backends, container orchestration nodes, mid-tier relational database systems, and distributed compilation pipelines.
